LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 1.3.1 VERB ‘TO BE’

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Language use 1.3.1 Verb ‘to be’
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language use 1.3.1 Verb ‘to be’, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we introduce ourselves? 2. How do we greet people in the morning/afternoon/ evening? 21 language e.g., how are you?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify the present tense forms of the verb ‘to be’ in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language use 1.3.1 Verb ‘to be’ in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use the present tense realisations of the verb ‘to be’ to greet and introduce oneself and others,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language use 1.3.1 Verb ‘to be’ in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. acknowledge the various present tense forms of the verb ‘to be’ in day-to-day communication. in day-to- day communication. ● Learners are guided to participate in language games and songs using present tense form of the verb ‘to be’. ● Learners with low vision watch while learners with blindness listen to audio-visual clips of children greeting one another and introducing themselves. Provide verbal descriptions of aspects of video that require the use of sight to the learners with blindness. ● Learners listen to their peers introduce themselves using the verb ‘to be.' Learners with blindness are given one on one description of the non-verbal cues as peers introduce themselves using the verb ‘to be’. ● In pairs, learners are guided to introduce themselves politely using the verb ‘to be’. ● Learners are guided to individually describe themselves and other people using the verb ‘to be’. ● Learners with low vision are guided to practise various types of greetings using appropriate 1. Learners with blindness be given one on one demonstrations and clear verbal instruction to practise various types of greetings using appropriate language e.g., how are you? I am fine. ● Learners are guided to role play various types of greetings using the verb ‘to be’.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language use 1.3.1 Verb ‘to be’ together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: A learner uses appropriate language structure (verb ‘to be’) to describe himself/herself, and other

people. Hence their ability to communicate is enhanced.

• Creativity and imagination: A learner role plays various types of greetings using the verb ‘to be’.

Values

Respect is enhanced the learner listens to one another introducing themselves in turns.

Values:

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self- esteem). The learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as they greet and introduces themselves and others.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learner links the concept of present tense form of the verb ‘to be’ to learning of similar concepts in Kiswahili languages activities.

Suggested learning resources

• Audio-visual clips

• Textbooks in appropriate font and colour contrast

• Braille reference materials
